info.name: S6 - Kubernetes Deployment
info.description: Skenario 6: Verifikasi deployment ke cluster Kubernetes (Minikube), HPA auto-scaling, Ingress routing, dan Istio traffic management

request.description:
S6 memerlukan: kubectl, minikube, atau cluster K8s yang sudah berjalan. Berikut langkah-langkah:

1. Start Minikube:
   minikube start --driver=docker --memory=4096 --cpus=2

2. Verifikasi cluster:
   kubectl version --client
   kubectl cluster-info

3. Create namespace:
   kubectl apply -f k8s/namespace.yaml

4. Setup secrets & configmap:
   kubectl apply -f k8s/secrets.yaml -n agricity
   kubectl apply -f k8s/configmap.yaml -n agricity

5. Deploy aplikasi:
   kubectl apply -k k8s/ -n agricity
   ATAU
   kubectl apply -f k8s/mysql-statefulset.yaml -n agricity
   kubectl apply -f k8s/rabbitmq-deployment.yaml -n agricity
   kubectl apply -f k8s/oauth-server-deployment.yaml -n agricity
   kubectl apply -f k8s/php-deployments.yaml -n agricity
   kubectl apply -f k8s/python-ml-deployment.yaml -n agricity
   kubectl apply -f k8s/gateway-deployment.yaml -n agricity

6. Setup port-forward:
   kubectl port-forward svc/gateway-service 3000:3000 -n agricity &
   kubectl port-forward svc/oauth-server-service 3002:3002 -n agricity &

7. Verifikasi pods:
   kubectl get pods -n agricity

Pastikan gateway pod sudah running melalui port-forward, lalu verify health

Command untuk melihat pods:
kubectl get pods -n agricity

Expected: Semua pods berstatus Running dengan READY = 1/1 (atau X/X untuk multi-container)
Test Gateway via Kubernetes service (port-forward ke svc/gateway-service 3000:3000)
Test OAuth Server via Kubernetes service (port-forward ke svc/oauth-server-service 3002:3002)

item.name: 6.4 - Login Test on K8s (OAuth via K8s)

request.description: Login via OAuth Server yang berjalan di Kubernetes
Test API Gateway di Kubernetes dengan token valid

Setup Istio (opsional untuk traffic management advanced):

1. Install Istio:
   curl -L https://github.com/istio/istio/releases/download/1.20.3/istio-1.20.3-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz
   cd istio-1.20.3
   ./bin/istioctl install --set profile=demo -y

   ATAU via Helm:
   helm repo add istio https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts
   helm install istio-base istio/base -n istio-system --create-namespace
   helm install istiod istio/istiod -n istio-system

2. Enable sidecar injection di namespace agricity:
   kubectl label namespace agricity istio-injection=enabled --overwrite

3. Restart pods:
   kubectl rollout restart deployment -n agricity

4. Apply Istio configs:
   kubectl apply -f k8s/istio/ -n agricity

5. Verify:
   kubectl get virtualservice -n agricity
   kubectl get destinationrule -n agricity
   kubectl get peerauthentication -n agricity

Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) Configuration:

1. View HPA status:
   kubectl get hpa -n agricity

   Expected output:
   NAME              REFERENCE                  TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
   agri-gateway-hpa  Deployment/agri-gateway    5%/80%    1         5         1
   php-farmer-hpa    Deployment/agri-php-farmer 3%/70%    1         3         1

2. View HPA details:
   kubectl describe hpa -n agricity

3. Monitor autoscaling (watch pods increase under load):
   kubectl get pods -n agricity -w

4. Generate load to trigger HPA (run in loop):
   for i in {1..100}; do
     curl -s -o /dev/null "http://localhost:3000/api/farmers" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
   done

5. Observe pod replicas increase as CPU/Memory hits threshold

Ingress Configuration for Smart AgriCity:

1. View Ingress:
   kubectl get ingress -n agricity

2. Describe Ingress:
   kubectl describe ingress -n agricity

3. For Minikube on Windows (Docker driver):
   - Direct IP access NOT available
   - Use port-forward INSTEAD:
     kubectl port-forward svc/gateway-service 3000:3000 -n agricity
   - Then access: http://localhost:3000

4. For Linux/Mac Minikube:
   - Optional: minikube tunnel (requires admin)
   - Then access via Ingress domain (e.g., http://agri.kelompok1.local/health)

5. Ingress paths configured:
   - /health → gateway
   - /api/farmers → farmer-service
   - /api/harvests → farmer-service
   - /api/irrigation/* → irrigation-service
   - /predict/* → python-ml-service
   - /oauth/* → oauth-server-service

Verify Kubernetes namespace:

Command:
kubectl get namespace agricity
kubectl get all -n agricity

Expected:
- Deployments: agri-gateway, agri-oauth-server, agri-php-farmer, agri-php-crop, agri-php-irrigation, agri-python-ml
- StatefulSets: agri-mysql
- Services: gateway-service, oauth-server-service, farmer-service, crop-service, irrigation-service, python-ml-service, mysql, rabbitmq
- Pods: All running
- HPA: hpa-gateway, hpa-php-farmer, etc.

MySQL StatefulSet with Persistent Volume:

Command:
kubectl get statefulset -n agricity
kubectl get pvc -n agricity

Expected:
- StatefulSet: agri-mysql (replicas 1)
- PersistentVolumeClaim: mysql-pvc (if using local storage)
- Data persists across pod restarts

To verify data persistence:
kubectl exec -it agri-mysql-0 -n agricity -- mysql -u root -psecret_db_password_change_me -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agriCity.frm_farmers;"

Service types in Smart AgriCity K8s:

1. View all services:
   kubectl get svc -n agricity

2. Service types configured:
   - gateway-service: ClusterIP (internal)
   - oauth-server-service: ClusterIP
   - farmer-service: ClusterIP
   - etc.

3. For external access on Minikube Windows:
   - Use port-forward (recommended)
   - LoadBalancer type NOT practical on local Minikube

4. To expose service externally (if needed):
   kubectl patch svc gateway-service -n agricity -p '{"spec":{"type":"LoadBalancer"}}'
   kubectl get svc -n agricity  # Check EXTERNAL-IP

   NOTE: On Minikube, LoadBalancer will show <pending> without tunnel

ConfigMap & Secrets management:

1. List ConfigMaps:
   kubectl get configmap -n agricity
   kubectl describe configmap agricity-config -n agricity

2. List Secrets (values redacted):
   kubectl get secret -n agricity
   kubectl describe secret agricity-secret -n agricity

3. To view actual secret value (CAUTION - sensitive data):
   kubectl get secret agricity-secret -n agricity -o jsonpath='{.data.db_password}' | base64 -d

4. Configuration mounted to pods as:
   - Environment variables
   - Volume mounts at /etc/config/ (ConfigMap)
   - Volume mounts at /etc/secret/ (Secrets)

Resource management for K8s deployments:

1. View resource requests/limits:
   kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n agricity

   Look for:
   Requests:
     cpu: 100m
     memory: 128Mi
   Limits:
     cpu: 500m
     memory: 512Mi

2. View node resource usage:
   kubectl top nodes
   kubectl top pod -n agricity

3. Resource allocation strategy:
   - Gateway: High CPU/Memory (frontend heavy)
   - OAuth Server: Medium
   - PHP services: Medium
   - Python ML: High (ML inference)
   - MySQL: High (database)
   - RabbitMQ: High (message broker)

Network Policies for security:

1. View network policies:
   kubectl get networkpolicy -n agricity

2. Example network policy (restrict traffic):
   Only allow traffic:
   - Gateway ↔ PHP services
   - PHP services ↔ MySQL
   - PHP services ↔ RabbitMQ
   - Deny all other

3. Apply custom network policy:
   kubectl apply -f <network-policy.yaml> -n agricity

   NOTE: Network Policies require CNI plugin support (flannel, calico, etc.)

Collect logs from Kubernetes pods:

1. View pod logs:
   kubectl logs <pod-name> -n agricity
   kubectl logs <pod-name> -n agricity --tail=50  # Last 50 lines
   kubectl logs <pod-name> -n agricity -f         # Follow logs (tail -f)

2. View logs from specific container (multi-container pod):
   kubectl logs <pod-name> -c <container-name> -n agricity

3. View previous pod logs (if pod crashed/restarted):
   kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous -n agricity

4. View logs for all pods in deployment:
   kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n agricity --tail=100

5. Export all logs:
   kubectl logs <pod-name> -n agricity > pod.log
   kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n agricity > gateway-logs.txt

Execute commands inside running pods:

1. Open shell in pod:
   kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n agricity -- /bin/bash
   kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n agricity -- /bin/sh  # Alpine images

2. Run single command in pod:
   kubectl exec <pod-name> -n agricity -- ls -la /app
   kubectl exec <pod-name> -n agricity -- ps aux

3. For MySQL pod:
   kubectl exec -it agri-mysql-0 -n agricity -- mysql -u root -psecret_db_password_change_me
   > SELECT * FROM agriCity.frm_farmers LIMIT 1;

4. Copy files from pod:
   kubectl cp agricity/<pod-name>:/path/to/file ./local-file -n agricity

5. Copy files to pod:
   kubectl cp ./local-file agricity/<pod-name>:/path/to/file -n agricity
